results.what: Administrative/historical statement: the Hannoverian triangulation (Gauss, 1820–1848) was already connected to the Danish (Schumacher), Dutch/French-English (Krayenhoff), Prussian (Müffling) and Hessian (Gerling) networks. The report therefore judges that joining the Prussian-led Central European Arc Measurement does not require re-triangulating Hanover.
results.modern_name: History of geodesy: Gauss's Hannoverian arc measurement and the founding of the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (1861/62, later the International Association of Geodesy)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Hannoverian triangulation); J. J. Baeyer (Central European Arc Measurement proposal, 1861)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely bureaucratic prose from a collective faculty report on the Prussian arc-measurement proposal and contains no mathematics. Riemann's involvement in such Göttingen committee reports is a minor biographical detail, not a mathematical result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the word at the line end reads 'Berichte' ('in der Anlage zu diesem Berichte'), possibly cut off at the margin; the transcription has 'Bericht'.

A long diagonal pencil stroke runs through the first five lines (from 'Überlegung' down to 'Motive'). There is also a slanted stroke in the left margin beside lines 3–5. These may be deletion or check marks and are not noted in the transcription.
A pencil folio number '69' appears in the right margin beside the line 'Hohes Curatorium ... Hochdemselben'.
'Krayenhof' is as written; the usual spelling of the Dutch geodesist's name is Krayenhoff (C. R. T. Krayenhoff).
The transcription is otherwise consistent with the image: 'Gauss', 'Schumacher', 'Ostfriesland, Oldenburg u. s. f. rectificirten', 'Müffling u. A.', 'Gerling'.
